title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: I is a 4-element set (in the elliptic-curve context, e.g. the four 2-torsion points or the four branch points of a level-2 structure). G = S_I ≅ S_4. V ⊂ S_I is the Klein four-group, and V* is its three non-trivial elements (the double transpositions). J = Π_22(I) is the 3-element set of partitions of I into two pairs, and S_I → S_J ≅ S_3 has kernel V. ω(X) denotes the two-element set of orientations of a finite set X (total orders modulo even permutations).

(1) Order-4 elements and the cube (marginal note (*) and first paragraph). The six 4-cycles u correspond to the six cyclic orders Circ(I) on I. They fall into three pairs {u, u^{-1}}, i.e. three cyclic subgroups of order 4. Since u² ∈ V*, squaring gives a 2:1 map Circ(I) → V*. Grothendieck reads this as a cube structure:
- I is the set of the 4 space diagonals.
- V* is the set of the 3 face directions (face axes).
- Circ(I) is the set of the 6 (suitably oriented) faces.
This is the classical identification of S_4 with the rotation group of the cube, acting on its diagonals. A 4-cycle is a quarter-turn about a face axis, and its square is the half-turn in V* about the same axis.

(2) Canonical isomorphism ω(I) ≃ ω(J). The signature identifies (S_I)_ab and (S_J)_ab with {±1}, compatibly with S_I → S_J. So ω(I) and ω(J) are torsors under the same group, and an S_I-equivariant isomorphism between them exists but is unique only up to the two choices. A concrete choice:
- Fix i ∈ I. Then I∖{i} ≅ J canonically, via j ↦ {{i,j}, complement}.
- A total order on I∖{i} extends to I by putting i first. This gives ω_i(I) ≃ ω(I∖{i}) ≃ ω(J).
- I checked that this is independent of i. With I = {1,2,3,4} and J = {a = 12|34, b = 13|24, c = 14|23}: i=1 gives (a,b,c), i=2 gives (c,a,b), i=3 gives (b,c,a), all the same orientation. Abstractly this follows from S_I-equivariance plus transitivity on I.
- Putting i last instead gives (c,b,a), the other isomorphism. This matches Grothendieck's remark about the 'convention contraire'.

(3) Bijections between three 3-element sets: V* ↔ {cyclic subgroups of order 4} ↔ {Sylow 2-subgroups (D_8)}.
- Γ ↦ the unique non-trivial element of Γ ∩ V.
- x ↦ N_G(⟨x⟩) = C_G(x), a Sylow 2-subgroup.
- D ↦ the non-trivial central element of D.

Purpose: to build a canonical, choice-free combinatorial dictionary for the S_4/S_3 symmetry of level-2 structures (the 4-set I versus the 3-set J of its pair-partitions). It also prepares 'polyhedral' combinatorial structures: cube here, combinatorial square on the next page.
errors: The first bottom diagram labels the map V* → {cyclic subgroups of order 4} as x ↦ Cent_G(x). But C_{S_4}((12)(34)) is dihedral of order 8 (a Sylow 2-subgroup), not cyclic of order 4. The second diagram appears to correct this by targeting the Sylow subgroups (via Norm/Cent) and going back via the centre of D.

Minor: the abelianization argument alone only yields an isomorphism ω(I) ≃ ω(J) up to two choices. The page correctly says so and fixes it by the 'i first' convention. That this convention is independent of i is not stated explicitly, but it is true.

ideas.what: S_4 as the rotation group of the cube: I = space diagonals, V* = face axes, 4-cycles = oriented faces, u ↦ u² a 2:1 map Circ(I) → V*
ideas.modern_name: Isomorphism of the octahedral rotation group with S_4

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism of orientation torsors ω(I) ≃ ω(Π_22(I)) for |I| = 4, made canonical by the 'i first' convention
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the sign characters under S_4 → S_3 (resolvent cubic / level-2 structures)

ideas.what: Bijections between double transpositions, cyclic subgroups of order 4 and Sylow 2-subgroups of S_4

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, classical combinatorics of S_4 and the cube, written in Grothendieck's characteristic 'canonical, choice-free' style. The only slightly nontrivial point is the canonical isomorphism of orientation sets ω(I) ≃ ω(J), which is folklore. Nothing new for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Margin start: likely 'On peut dire aussi que les six éléments d'ordre 4 se répartissent en trois paires {u,u^{-1}} correspondant aux trois sous-groupes cycliques d'ordre 4 de G = S_I, i.e. en bijection avec V*', followed by 'I est l'ens. des quatre diagonales des cubes'.
'ω_1(I)' should read 'ω_i(I)' (dependent on the chosen i ∈ I).

The line transcribed '≃ Γ_total Σ l'ordre total de I' probably reads: to a total order on I∖{i}, associate the total order on I which induces the given order on I∖{i} and has i as first element. The 'Γ' is likely I∖{i}, and the target is presumably ω(J) via I∖{i} ≅ J.
'S_{I ab} → S_{J ab} ≃ {±1}': the subscripts are abelianizations (S_I)_ab and (S_J)_ab.
In the bottom diagrams: 'x ↦ Norm' (normalizer of ⟨x⟩), and 'D ↦ élément non trivial du centre de D', with target 'Ss-groupes de Sylow de G = S_I'.
